thread:
alex: Hey team — Mercurial Health (enterprise POC) wants streaming + function-calls + strict tabular JSON output they can ingest into their analytics pipeline. They're worried about per-token costs during live calls. Any quick checklist?
priya: Nice — do they require SSO / dedicated tenancy?
alex: Yes SAML + customer needs keys in their KMS, plus SOC2 attestation. They're open to Dedicated but want a cost estimate for hosted first.
ben: Sales note — they have ~200 concurrent streams during peak, avg 30s responses, spikes to 800 in promos. Need SLA on latency (p95 < 300ms).
priya: For structured output, recommend using function-calling/JSON schema to keep shape deterministic. Send them an example schema and we can lock model + tokens.
taylor: One runtime heads-up: continuous KV cache + streaming may cause prefix cache mismatch if clients do incremental tool calls. We had an edgecase where mixed function-call responses broke the CSV formatter.
alex: Is that the same bug from last month where tool-called content wasn't appended to the prefix? Could cause missing rows.
taylor: Yep. Patch queued but not on prod Dedicated clusters yet. Workaround: disable KV prefix caching for those streams or use short-lived cache TTL. That increases token counts ~8–12% depending on overlap.
priya: For cost math: if avg response = 300 tokens and 200 concurrent * 30s => estimate qps. Quick calc: 200 streams * (300 tokens / 30s) = 2000 tokens/sec => ~7.2M tokens/hr. If hosted price = $0.0005 per 1k input + $0.001 per 1k output (example), that's approx $5.4/hr at baseline? Wait I'm off — lemme do an inline calc.
priya: ```
# rough
streams = 200
avg_tokens_per_resp = 300
responses_per_min_per_stream = 2
per_min_tokens = streams * avg_tokens_per_resp * responses_per_min_per_stream
# 200*300*2 = 120k tokens/min = 7.2M tokens/hr
# cost @ $0.001 per 1k output = 7.2k * $0.001 = $7.2/hr
```
ben: Good. We should present hosted baseline + delta for Dedicated (flat monthly + lower unit). Ops also need to see burst capacity charges.
alex: On the schema side they asked for a SQL-like row output, e.g., array of objects with typed fields. Example they want: id, timestamp, intent, confidence, entities JSON.
priya: Recommend this function signature to guarantee shape: ```
function emit_row(records: List[Record]) -> JSON:
  Record = {"id": string, "ts": string, "intent": string, "confidence": number, "entities": object}
```
priya: Then set function-calling strict mode so model returns only the function payload.
taylor: Note: streaming + function-calling requires us to buffer function params until end of call on some runtime configs. If they need true token-level streaming of partial JSON rows we might need to fallback to chunked newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) approach. That trades off parseability for latency.
alex: They've explicitly asked for "streaming rows as they come" to our webhook. Is NDJSON acceptable?
priya: Ask the customer — many analytics ingesters accept NDJSON. If not, we can implement a deterministic row-commit delimiter, e.g., "\u241E" (record separator) to avoid JSON boundary ambiguity.
ben: Legal / security: KMS integration required for Private deploy. For hosted we can do envelope encryption but they likely won't accept that. Lead with hosted for evaluation, promise Private/Dedicated plan in contract.
alex: Any blockers for demo tomorrow? I need a quick runbook to hand to Mercurial CTO about expected incompatibilities and suggested configs.
priya: Runbook bullet points: 1) Use strict function-calling. 2) If you need per-row streaming, prefer NDJSON with record delimiter. 3) Turn off prefix KV cache or set TTL=2s for live streams to avoid stale tool outputs. 4) Provide traffic profile for cost estimate. 5) SAML + KMS onboard steps (link).
taylor: I'll add a runtime note: if they elect to keep KV caching, we can enable model-variant fallback with a consistency flag, but cost may rise and latency jitter can increase ~10-20ms.
ben: I'll prepare pricing slide with Hosted vs Dedicated numbers and expected savings at scale. alex — share the customer's projected qps and retention window.
alex: Shared in DM. Also they sent a security questionnaire with a question about offloading PII to external tool calls. They want confirmation PII won't be cached externally.
priya: We should confirm: by default we do not surface customer interaction to 3rd party tools. If they call their own internal tool via function-call, data flows to that tool. We must document responsibility.
alex: Noted. I'll flag that to legal.
deploy-bot: CI pipeline finished: canary runtime with cache-ttl toggle deployed to staging (build #4821). :rocket:
priya: Awesome — can we deploy the KV-ttl toggle to a demo sandbox so Mercurial can test both behaviors?
taylor: Yes — I can provision a sandbox and enable the toggle. Expect a sandbox URL in ~2 hours.
alex: Perfect. I'll update the customer and book a 30-min demo to show NDJSON and function-call proof-of-concept.
ben: I'll draft the commercial note: 30-day hosted eval credit, option to convert to Dedicated with 30% unit-cost reduction after commit.
priya: Action items: alex (customer comms & SAML/KMS questionnaire), taylor (sandbox + KV TTL toggle), ben (pricing slide + contract language)
alex: Thanks all — ping if anything else. :thumbsup:
